issues.legal_issue: An eviction suit based on the landlord’s own-occupation requirement is incompetent when instituted within the statutory waiting period after the landlord acquires the property.
material_facts: The landlord acquired the property by transfer on March 13, 1963, and filed the eviction suit on June 23, 1964, less than three years later.
The eviction decree was also based on the landlord’s claim that the premises were reasonably required for personal occupation.
issues.conclusion: The suit was incompetent when instituted, so the eviction decree on the own-occupation ground was set aside. The landlord was given liberty to bring a fresh suit on the amended own-occupation ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(3A) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act bars a suit on the grounds in Section 13(1)(f) or (ff) until three years after the landlord acquires the interest by transfer. The provision applies retrospectively and is constitutional, as held in Banerjee v Anita Pawar (1975) 2 SCR 774. A claim under the amended Section 13(1)(ff) may be brought afresh, with its merits assessed on the evidence in that suit.

predicates.eviction_suit_based_on_own_occupation: The landlord brought an eviction proceeding relying on the premises being reasonably required for personal occupation.
predicates.landlord_acquired_interest_by_transfer: The landlord acquired the interest in the premises by transfer.
predicates.suit_filed_within_waiting_period: The landlord filed the eviction suit before the required waiting period after acquiring the interest had expired.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings an own-occupation eviction suit after acquiring the premises by transfer but before the waiting period expires, the decree on that ground must be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A decree for eviction based on subletting requires proof that the subletting occurred after the applicable law commenced and without the landlord’s consent.
material_facts: The landlord alleged that the tenant sublet part of the premises after the tenancy law commenced.

In an earlier proceeding, the Rent Controller found that the subletting had occurred before that law commenced and with the written consent of the original owner; the owner’s successor was bound by that determination.
The landlord had no personal knowledge of the subletting, and the evidence did not establish that it occurred after the law commenced.
The tenant had not admitted, and had not been asked in cross-examination, whether the subletting occurred after commencement.
issues.conclusion: The post-commencement subletting required to sustain eviction was not proved. The eviction decree on the subletting ground could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(a) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act makes subletting a ground for eviction when it occurs after the Act’s commencement without the landlord’s previous written consent. Sections 16(1)–(3) govern notice and the consequences of sublettings created after or before commencement. A determination in an earlier proceeding to which the landlord’s predecessor-in-title was a party could not be reopened by the successor. The court also relied on the absence of evidence establishing post-commencement subletting.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding_based_on_subletting and subletting_predated_law_commencement and prior_determination_bound_successor and not evidence_of_post_commencement_subletting

predicates.eviction_proceeding_based_on_subletting: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the tenant sublet all or part of the premises.
predicates.subletting_predated_law_commencement: The subletting occurred before the relevant tenancy law commenced.
predicates.prior_determination_bound_successor: An earlier proceeding involving the landlord’s predecessor determined the relevant fact, and that determination bound the successor landlord.
predicates.evidence_of_post_commencement_subletting: Evidence established that the subletting occurred after the relevant tenancy law commenced.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding rests on subletting that predated the relevant law, an earlier determination binds the successor landlord, and there is no evidence of later subletting, the eviction decree on that ground must be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: When an own-occupation eviction claim was brought prematurely and the relevant circumstances must be assessed afresh, liberty to bring a new suit is preferable to remanding the old claim.
material_facts: About twenty years had passed since the suit was instituted.
The landlord’s entitlement under the amended own-occupation ground had to be assessed in light of the circumstances existing at the time of a fresh trial and on evidence adduced there.
issues.conclusion: The court declined to remand the matter and instead granted liberty to file a fresh suit on the amended own-occupation ground, leaving the merits to be determined afresh.
issues.legal_principle: Where substantial time has passed and the claim depends on the circumstances and evidence relevant at the time of trial, the court may decline remand and permit a fresh suit so that the claim is examined on the current circumstances. The court applied this approach to a fresh claim under Section 13(1)(ff) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act.

predicates.premature_own_occupation_claim: The landlord’s own-occupation eviction claim was brought before the required waiting period had expired.
predicates.substantial_time_elapsed: A substantial period passed after the original suit was instituted.
predicates.current_circumstances_require_fresh_evid: The claim’s merits depend on current circumstances that must be examined through evidence at trial.

issues.definition: When an own-occupation claim was premature, substantial time has passed, and current circumstances require fresh evidence, liberty to file a new suit is granted instead of remanding the old claim.
